## Answer
A React SPA needs no client secret: use MSAL Browser with authorization code + PKCE, appropriate redirect URIs and account audience. Keep secrets and private keys out of browser code; do not enable implicit grant.
API consent authorizes API access: delegated permissions act for a signed-in user; application permissions act without one. Consent requirements depend on the permission and tenant policy. Azure RBAC governs resource access through scoped roles; it does not replace API consent or grant directory administration.
Later, identify the target cloud, tenant, subscription, environment, hosting platform, API operations and approving owners. These choices do not block this explanation.
For CI, discuss workload identity federation, or managed identity where the host supports it; use certificate authentication when appropriate if federation is unavailable. Treat client secrets as a deliberate fallback.
For certificates, register the public certificate with Entra and securely retain the private signing key. Plan expiry, storage, rotation overlap and retirement; TLS certificates serve a different purpose.
For a future explicitly authorized human session, discuss browser sign-in, MFA, subscription selection and a minimal scoped access check. Azure CLI and azd sessions are separate; login alone proves neither permissions nor deployment success.
This is informational only: no login, tenant connection, credential creation, permission grant or deployment was performed.
